definition: Relating to a form of cell-to-cell signaling where a ligand on one cell binds directly to a receptor on an adjacent cell.
etymology: From Latin juxta ('near, adjacent') + Greek κρίνειν (krínein, 'to separate, secrete').
manuscriptExample: Notch receptor signaling operates via juxtacrine interaction between neighboring membrane-bound proteins.
conferenceExample: The reviewer inquired whether paracrine factors could be excluded in favor of purely juxtacrine communication.

definition: The act or placement of two elements or biological structures side by side to highlight comparison or contrast.
etymology: From Latin juxta ('next to') + French position.
manuscriptExample: The structural juxtaposition of wild-type and mutant active sites illuminated key catalytic differences.
conferenceExample: In Figure 4, side-by-side juxtaposition of immunofluorescence channels clearly demonstrated co-localization.
